open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text:
The same refusal answers a
   failure to open or lock the lock file, which waiting for another holder is not, and a mark that cannot be
   written.
open_points.question: Does the preceding guarantee that the operation "changes no record and no stored image" apply to an unwritable mark, and at which failed step—temporary-file creation, writing, file synchronisation, rename, or folder synchronisation—must the operation preserve or roll back the old state?
options: Every failed step returns STATE_UNAVAILABLE and leaves no new or changed record or stored image.
Only the refusal code carries into this sentence; a mark already renamed before a later synchronisation failure may remain.
The rename commits the mark, so a failure after rename is success rather than STATE_UNAVAILABLE.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the no-change guarantee to every STATE_UNAVAILABLE case and treat the mark as committed only after folder synchronisation succeeds.

witness.initial: A placement exists, no publication mark exists, and the state folder permits creating, writing, synchronising, and renaming the temporary mark file but its folder synchronisation fails.
events: The calling flow asks the deliverer to record a publication mark.
The deliverer renames the completed temporary file to the final mark name.
outcomes: The deliverer returns STATE_UNAVAILABLE and removes or otherwise makes the new mark unavailable, preserving the prior state.
The deliverer returns STATE_UNAVAILABLE but leaves the renamed mark in place because the rule carries only the refusal into the mark-write case or because rename already committed it.
witness.observer: The calling flow on the refusal and a later mark or scan that either finds or does not find the mark.

open_points.subject: A6
open_points.text: changes no record and no stored image
open_points.question: Which formal invariant and Required tests item require showing that every refusal covered by this changed guarantee leaves every record and stored image unchanged, including an unwritable mark?
options: Extend INV-20 and its Required tests item to assert that all records and stored images remain unchanged for every A6 rule 5 refusal.
Add a separate formal invariant and Required tests item for refusal atomicity.
Limit the normative guarantee to the damaged record case already partially covered by INV-20.
open_points.default_guess: Extend INV-20 and require before-and-after assertions over all records and stored images for every A6 rule 5 refusal.

open_points.subject: A6
open_points.question: What source supplies `marked_at`, what exact datetime representation and UTC/offset convention is stored, and how many readings of that source may one mark operation take?
options: Inject a clock, read it exactly once for a newly created mark, and store an aware UTC datetime.
Inject a clock, read it exactly once, and store UTC without an offset.
Read ambient system time inside the operation, with representation chosen by the implementation.
open_points.default_guess: Inject a clock, read it exactly once only when creating a new mark, and store an aware UTC datetime; replay preserves the stored value.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a mark, and the clock can return two distinguishable instants.
events: The calling flow records the first publication mark.
The deliverer creates M07 and persists `marked_at`.
The mark is later read or replayed.
outcomes: The stored value is the single injected-clock reading in aware UTC form.
The implementation uses ambient time, another reading, or a UTC datetime without an offset.
witness.observer: A caller or record reader that receives or inspects the mark and its `marked_at` value.

open_points.subject: context
open_points.text:
every
operation on a project needs the token
open_points.question: Is a request to a project-scoped operation considered "on a project" before its project id is validated or resolved, so that token checking always precedes malformed-id, unknown-project, and connection checks for scan, delivery, and mark?
options: Every invocation of a project-scoped operation requires and checks the token first, even when the project id is malformed or unknown.
The token is required only after the request identifies an existing project.
Each operation chooses its own precedence.
open_points.default_guess: Treat every invocation of scan, delivery, or mark as project-scoped and check the token before validating or resolving the project id.

witness.initial: The caller has no token and supplies a malformed project id to a scan or mark request.
events: The caller invokes the project-scoped operation.
The service evaluates whether the request is an operation on a project.
outcomes: The service refuses for the missing token before examining the project id.
The service reports the malformed or unresolved project first because no project was identified.
witness.observer: The caller sees a different refusal and learns whether project validation occurs without authentication.
